title: Aliasing Demonstrator
description: A true sine wave with sample dots and a reconstructed curve that diverges into a slower ghost frequency, turning red the moment the Nyquist limit is crossed.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Sampling Theory
Signals and Systems

learningObjectives: Examine how sampling rate and true frequency determine the reconstruction
Distinguish correct sampling from aliased sampling
prerequisites: A sine wave has a frequency
Sampling records values at discrete instants

controls.label: Show reconstructed (aliased) curve
controls.purpose: Draw the signal the samples actually describe

assumptions: Ideal instantaneous sampling with no aperture time or jitter
A single pure sinusoid with zero starting phase
limitations: Real converters include an anti-aliasing filter that attenuates above-Nyquist content before it can fold

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Parameter exploration with a hard-boundary color state change
keyQuestions: At what frequency does the readout turn red, and why exactly there?
Can the system tell from the samples alone that they are wrong?
commonMisconceptions: That aliasing degrades quality gradually rather than producing a specific wrong frequency
That aliasing can be filtered out after sampling
assessmentOpportunities: Compute the apparent frequency for a 5 kHz tone sampled at 8 kHz
